description: Composite two-panel micrograph figure of the air-cooled hot-rolled Fe-9Mn-6Al-0.15C alloy (composite group: one optical micrograph plus one SEM micrograph). (a) is an optical micrograph with a 100 µm scale bar and a double-headed "Rolling direction" arrow at top right; it shows a strongly banded, elongated (rolling-direction aligned) structure in which bright white regions are labelled δ, darker speckled regions are labelled γ, and mottled grey lath-like regions are labelled α'+α+γ. (b) is an SEM micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar and the same rolling-direction annotation, resolving the interior of the lath-like constituent: dark featureless regions labelled γ (upper centre) and δ (lower left), a region of fine interleaved laths labelled α', and small bright globular particles labelled α, pointed out by two white arrows. Together the panels argue that the hot-rolled air-cooled microstructure consists of partially recrystallized δ-ferrite bands plus γ-austenite and lath-like α'-martensite containing small globular α-ferrite particles: (a) gives the phase distribution over hundreds of micrometres, (b) the sub-micrometre detail inside the lath-like phase. Apart from the scale bars and phase labels, no numeric values are printed on either panel.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph, 100 µm scale bar, double-headed "Rolling direction" arrow top right. Banded/elongated structure with bright white regions labelled δ, dark speckled regions labelled γ, and mottled grey lath-like regions labelled α'+α+γ. Phases are elongated roughly parallel to the rolling direction; no grain-boundary or precipitate detail resolvable at this magnification.

SEM micrograph, 10 µm scale bar, "Rolling direction" arrow top right. Shows the interior of the lath-like phase: dark featureless areas labelled γ (top centre) and δ (bottom left), a fine lath packet labelled α', and small globular particles labelled α indicated by two white arrows embedded among the laths.

observations.observation: (a) is an optical micrograph carrying a 100 µm scale bar and a double-headed arrow labelled "Rolling direction" at its top right corner.
(a) shows elongated, banded phases aligned approximately parallel to the rolling direction, with bright white bands alternating with darker speckled and mottled grey lath-like regions.
(a) carries three printed phase labels: δ on the bright white regions, γ on dark speckled regions, and α'+α+γ on the mottled lath-like regions.
(b) is an SEM micrograph carrying a 10 µm scale bar and the same double-headed "Rolling direction" annotation as (a).
(b) resolves a lath-like constituent made of fine interleaved laths labelled α', with two white arrows pointing to small globular particles labelled α within/across the lath packet.
In (b) two dark, featureless regions are labelled γ (upper centre) and δ (lower left); at the supplied resolution their grey levels are similar and the distinction relies on the printed labels.
The caption identifies the figure as the microstructure of the air-cooled hot-rolled specimen of the Fe-9Mn-6Al-0.15C alloy [53].
The caption states that the optical microstructure (a) is composed of partially recrystallized δ-ferrite (white), γ-austenite (brown) and other lath-like phases (grey).
The caption states that the SEM image (b) shows the details inside the lath-like phase, consisting of γ-austenite, a lath-like martensite α' and small globular ferrite α-particles.

The citing text states that in Fe-(9-12)Mn-6Al-(0.15-0.3)C alloys the air-cooled hot-rolled microstructure consists of partially recrystallized δ-ferrite, γ-austenite and minor constituents such as γ_retained austenite, lath-like α'-martensite and small globular α-ferrite particles inside the lath-like phase, as shown in Fig. 20.
The citing text states that no precipitates of κ-carbide are observed in the air-cooled hot-rolled samples — a claim this figure's panels cannot confirm or refute at the supplied resolution.
The citing text states that the amount of martensite (α') decreases as the Mn or C content is increased; this figure shows a single composition and therefore does not itself demonstrate the trend.
No numeric values other than the scale bars (100 µm in (a), 10 µm in (b)), the phase labels and the rolling-direction arrows are printed on either panel.
